title: upgrade-attn-flashattnv2-rope-rotary-fused-kv-batching-scheduling
author: Aisha Kapoor
body:
Motivation: Upgrade attention kernels to use the v2 FlashAttention implementation with fused rotary/rope ops and tighter KV-cache-aware batching and scheduling. This change reduces kernel launch overhead, enables fused rotary/rope computation paths, and introduces scheduling hints so the runtime can prefer fused kernels for supported model configs. The PR contains three workstreams in one landing: 1) kernel integration and guardrails, 2) runtime scheduling + capability detection, 3) KV-cache batching improvements and fallbacks.

Summary of changes: - Integrate FlashAttentionV2 kernels with fused rotary/rope support and optimized memory layouts. - Add detection of model rotary/rope patterns and route them to fused kernels when available. - Extend the scheduler with a "preferred_kernel" hint and cost-model weights to bias selection toward fused kernels for typical sequence lengths. - Continuous-batching: add KV-cache-aware batch slicing so cached prefixes don't force full matrix recompute; improves throughput for generation workloads with long histories. - Add unit and integration tests, microbench harness, and end-to-end perf script used for validation.

Checklist: - [x] Kernel API integration + build flags - [x] Runtime detection and routing - [x] Fallbacks for older GPUs / unsupported dims - [x] Benchmarks + perf regression DAG - [x] Review comments resolved

Performance summary (internal microbench, A100s, mixed sequence lengths): - Throughput: +1.4x end-to-end tokens/s on 8k-sequence workloads (medium-latency mode) - Latency: p99 generation latency down ~18% on 512-2048 prompt ranges - Memory: ~12% lower peak activation memory for fused kernels enabling +20% larger batch sizes in some configs - KV-cache hit path: 5-12% additional throughput improvement for workloads with high cache-hit rates.

Compatibility & fallbacks: The code paths include capability checks at startup (compute capability, supported tensor shapes) and runtime guards. When fused kernels are not compatible, scheduler falls back to existing FlashAttention fallback path. There are also environment flags (REDWOOD_FORCE_FUSED_ATTN, REDWOOD_DISABLE_FUSED_ATTN) for QA/rollout.

Related linear tickets: ENG-4765 (flashattn-v2 integration), ENG-4820 (scheduling heuristics). References: upstream flashattn@v2.3.1, internal design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4765/flashattn-v2-integration (internal).

Files changed (high level): runtime/attn/flashattn_v2_integration.cpp, runtime/attn/fused_rotary.cu, runtime/scheduler/kernel_selector.cc, runtime/scheduler/cost_model.h, runtime/kv_cache/batching.cpp, build/third_party/flashattn/README.md, tests/attn/flashattn_v2_smoke_test.py, perf/microbench/flashattn_v2_bench.py, docs/release/notes/2025-02-attn-upgrade.md.

Notes on testing: Unit tests cover fused vs unfused numerical equality within tolerance on fp16/amp. Integration tests run model runner (gpt-3-like) with and without fused kernels and assert throughput/regression thresholds. Perf harness contains reproducible steps to measure throughput/latency and is included under perf/microbench.

Migration / rollout plan: Start rollout on dedicated clusters flagged as "canary-fused-kernels" for 72 hours. Monitor p99 latency, token/cost breakdown, and tail OOM counts. If metrics are stable, expand to auto-roll for production clusters.

Why this matters: This PR reduces per-token cost by both improving kernel efficiency and enabling larger effective batching while preserving latency SLOs via scheduler heuristics. The fused-rotary/rope path is particularly beneficial for long-context models where rotary embeddings are used extensively.
commits: a1b2c3d: add initial bindings for FlashAttentionV2 and build integration
d4e5f6a: implement fused_rotary CUDA kernels with vectorized loads
b7c8d9e: scheduler: add preferred_kernel hint and cost weights
c0ffee1: kv_cache: add batch slicing for cached prefixes
f1e2d3c: tests: add smoke/integration/perf harness and CI job
deadbeef: docs: release notes and rollout plan
review_comments: Lena Park: Can we add a runtime guard for unsupported SMs (e.g. SM<8.0)? also prefer explicit fallback path so we don't accidentally pick fused kernels on an unsupported GPU.
Author (Aisha Kapoor): Added compute-capability guard and config flag REDWOOD_DISABLE_FUSED_ATTN; also added unit test to simulate unsupported devices.
Rafael Ortega: The cost model weights look reasonable but please add a small ablation in the perf harness to show schedulerChooser decisions at different seq-lens.
Author: Added ablation script and included sample output in perf/microbench/ablation_results.md (summary in PR body).
Connor Blake: Minor comment — ensure legal/third-party attribution files are included for upstream FlashAttention.
Author: Added build/third_party/flashattn/README.md and LICENSE note; CI now exposes a legal check step.
ci_checks: perf: microbench smoke — PASS (bench artifacts uploaded)
perf_tests: microbench: 8k-seq A100 x8; baseline vs fused: +1.4x throughput
producer-consumer: mixed seqs 256-4096 real workload: p99 -18%
merge_outcome: Merged via squash and merge after 2 approvals. No conflicts. Rollout gate set to canary clusters; merge commit includes changelog and rollout doc.
release_notes: Attention kernels upgraded to FlashAttentionV2 with fused rotary/rope ops, scheduler heuristics to prefer fused kernels, and KV-cache-aware batching. Expected: ~1.4x throughput on long sequences, improved p99 latency, and lower activation memory in many configs. Rollout is canary-first. See docs/release/notes/2025-02-attn-upgrade.md for details.
notes: This PR was sensitive to numerical equivalence — we accepted a max rel error of 1e-3 for fp16 paths after investigation. The perf harness and artifacts are uploaded under perf/artifacts/540123/.
